problem:
Let $⟨-1,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+ky=-4 \\ 3x-4y=5.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-2|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$
- $|\begin{aligned}2 & k \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}|=-|\begin{aligned}-4 & k \\ 5 & -4\end{aligned}|$

activity_context.topic_title: Cramer's Rule for 2x2 Systems of Linear Equations

feedback.problem:
Let $⟨x,1⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-y=k \\ x+4y=3\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

- $|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|=5$
- $|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|=-7$
- $|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|=13$
feedback.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =12+1 \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 1 & =\frac{|\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|}{13} \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & k \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & =13\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".
